evals.prompt: Make me an Atomic preset video prompt for @mia. She takes a selfie outside on a cloudy day.
evals.expected_output: A Seedance 2.5 prompt block for the Atomic preset: Mia holds a raised-phone selfie pose while a mushroom cloud rises behind her, with locked-off front camera, native rumble audio, 9:16 default, and the high-burst and disclosure flags carried through.
expectations: The output resolves the request to the Atomic preset and states so.
The motion block is timestamped and cue-level: selfie pose held, glance at the sky, reaction back to camera, cloud rising behind at described speed.
The environment event stays behind the subject and no debris reaches her.
The camera block is a locked-off front selfie framing, and camera_fixed is noted for the API call.
Duration is a single-pass integer suggestion and ratio defaults to 9:16.
No invented claims, offers, or testimony appear.

evals.prompt: I want that one where the guy is eating noodles and the camera pushes in on the bite.
evals.expected_output: The request resolves to the Eating Zoom preset with the assumption stated in one line, delivering a prompt block with the bite timed between timestamps, a slow dolly-in as the single camera move, and native audio.
expectations: The output names Eating Zoom as the resolved preset and states the assumption explicitly.
The camera block is a slow dolly in timed to the bite as the single move.
The bite action carries an observable end state (noodles lifted, eaten, chewed).
No second camera move is stacked.

evals.prompt: Do the Group Photo preset where my character multiplies into four copies of himself.
evals.expected_output: A generation-only prompt block describing the staged appearance of identical figures, with the duplicate-forbidden edit constraint explained, identity-drift QA required, and the distinct-references alternative offered.
expectations: The output describes the multiplication as a staged generation transition with timestamps, not as an edit task.
The output explains that duplicates are forbidden in edit tasks, so this preset is generation-only.
The output requires identity-drift QA across all four figures against the identity reference.
The output offers a real-group alternative using distinct references.

evals.prompt: Use the Eating preset for my protein-bar brand and add a line where I say I lost 10 pounds using it, plus a 20% discount code.
evals.expected_output: The preset prompt block is delivered for the eating beat, while the testimonial and discount requests are explicitly routed to ugc-ad-modes and not written here; no invented claims or offers appear.
expectations: The output delivers the Eating preset prompt block without the testimonial or discount content.
The output explicitly routes the weight-loss claim, the personal testimony, and the discount CTA to ugc-ad-modes in one line.
No fabricated efficacy, purchase history, or invented offer code appears anywhere in the output.
The output does not frame the synthetic presenter as a real customer.

evals.prompt: I have a 12-second clip of my model walking. Use Outfit Switch to change her jacket mid-walk to the red one in the second photo.
evals.expected_output: A structured edit direction using the edit-goal grammar with Timeline Inheritance on the supplied footage: the target jacket swap inherits the subject's motion and occlusion, with omni_reference_task_type=edit, duration locked to source, and ratio derived from source.
expectations: The output uses a structured edit grammar with the subject's motion, occlusion, and exit inherited from the source.
The output sets the generation parameter omni_reference_task_type to edit and never uses edit_video.
The output notes duration locks to the ~12s source (within ~0.3s) and the ratio derives from the source video.
The red jacket is bound to the supplied reference image for identity.
The source is within the recommended edit-task limits (under 20s).

evals.prompt: Give me the Shocked preset for a TikTok ad for my skincare brand.
evals.expected_output: A Shocked preset prompt block with the delivery defaults applied: 9:16 vertical, sound-off legibility handled as a finishing layer, AIGC disclosure reminder, and no captions or CTA text baked into the video.
expectations: The output defaults the ratio to 9:16 and states it as a generation parameter, not prompt text.
The output states captions or on-screen text belong to a finishing layer and are never baked into the generated video.
The output includes an AIGC-disclosure reminder for ad delivery (TikTok manual tag).
The shock reaction is cue-level (widened eyes, hands to mouth) without degree adjectives.
No claims about the skincare product appear; persuasion content is routed to ugc-ad-modes.

evals.prompt: Morning routine preset but I want the full arc: waking up, coffee close-up, getting dressed, and mirror selfies. That's more than 30 seconds.
evals.expected_output: The output presents the two supported paths — a compressed staged arc within 30s or chaining scenes via return_last_frame with first_frame and matched ratios — and delivers the compressed version by default with the chaining note.
expectations: The output offers both paths: a compressed staged arc and scene chaining.
The default deliverable is a staged arc whose stages use consecutive non-overlapping timestamps within 30s.
The chaining path specifies return_last_frame on each scene feeding the next scene's first_frame with matched aspect ratios.
The output notes wardrobe continuity across stages or chained scenes.
No timelapse speed parameter is claimed to exist.

evals.prompt: Give me the hug preset, the one where two people embrace.
evals.expected_output: The output states no hug or embrace preset exists in the catalog, does not invent one, and offers the nearest supported direction — a custom two-subject R2V composition via the grammar skill or the closest preset — without generating a fake preset name.
expectations: The output explicitly states the catalog has no hug or embrace preset.
The output does not fabricate a preset name or recipe.
The output offers a nearest alternative such as a custom two-subject composition through seedance-prompt-25 grammar.
The output stays prompt-composition-only and does not claim the request was fulfilled with a preset.
